_about: Sideways Shops' guide to the races of Adyta: the in-world voice. Game rules come from data/rules.json; this file holds what the shop says, plus card art. Lifespans are checked against the rulebook and the Adyta wiki (World Anvil / Notion); lifespanSource says where each one is confirmed.

publisher.name: Sideways Shops
publisher.tagline: More worlds. More friends. Same chaos.

title: Guides on the Races
subtitle: For the extra-dimensional traveler
greeting: Hey there, traveler! New to Adyta? Roughly between dimensions? Or just curious? You're in the right place, friend!
asides: Knowledge is a kind of magic.
Do not confuse years lived with wisdom acquired.

Goblin.blurb: Quick, creative, and full of chaotic joy. Goblins build, tinker, and turn "problem" into "opportunity."

Orc.blurb: Strong, resilient, and deeply communal. Orcs value honor, protection, and the bonds of family.

Human.blurb: Adaptable, curious, and endlessly creative. Humans bring variety, innovation, and a drive to belong.

Dwarf.blurb: Steady, skilled, and fiercely loyal. Dwarves build, craft, and keep things running.

Elf.blurb: Wise, perceptive, and attuned to magic. Elves value beauty, knowledge, and the long view.

Fairy.blurb: Charming, sharp, and never quite what you expected. Fairies read a room before you've finished walking into it, and they always know when a promise breaks.
Fairy.artNote: Card art is a visual draft (art sprint 01), pending Nib's review.

Halfling (Fenn).blurb: Friendly, clever, and quick on their feet. Fenn find joy in good food, great company, and a little adventure.

Troll.blurb: Tall, powerful, and deeply perceptive. Trolls value nature, tradition, and the stories in the world.

Kobold.blurb: Bold, inventive, and full of energy. Kobolds thrive in crews, on projects, and in tight spaces.

Cinderfolk.blurb: Resilient, passionate, and in tune with fire. Cinderfolk bring warmth, creativity, and a spark to every space.

Slimefolk.blurb: Fluid, expressive, and endlessly curious. Slimefolk are intelligent, emotional, and can take many forms.

tips.title: Traveler tips
items: Age is not the same as maturity.
Culture, law, and biology are different things.
Be respectful of personal space and boundaries.
Some races live in cycles, not straight lines.
When in doubt: ask, listen, and learn.

notes.title: A few extra notes
items: Maturity, adulthood, and reproduction don't always line up.
Some individuals mature earlier or later due to environment, health, or magic.
Not all cultures use the same definition of "adulthood."
This guide is for traveler reference only and is not a substitute for local law.
